subject: Why is apply slower in Shiny than in R?

messages.author: 96a4082f806e46f4
messages.subject: Why is apply slower in Shiny than in R?
parts:
Greetings,

I am new to Shiny and creating a sampling distribution demonstration for the ANOVA F-test.  In my app the user will click a button to simulate data from a specified distribution.  The data are plotted and the F-statistic is added to a histogram of F-statistics.  The user can simulate repeated samples, augmenting the F-statistic histogram, and the user can also simulate up to 1000 samples at a time.

What I found is that the apply function which works so fast in R is a lot slower in Shiny.  This means that applying a function to extract the F-statistics from a matrix of simulated data is much slower than I would like, so the user needs to wait several seconds after requesting results for 1000 simulated data sets.

The below ui and server have hopefully minimal code (plots excluded) to show what is going on.  I wrote a comment above the one line that slows down the code.  If you comment out that line, and request 1000 samples, your request is processed instantly, but without commenting out that line, it takes 3-4 seconds.  I would love any insight into why this process is so slow and whether there are ways it can be sped up.  


shinyUI(fluidPage(

  titlePanel("ANOVA F-test"),
  fluidRow(
    column(3,
           wellPanel( 
             h5("Specifications for ANOVA:"),
             br(),
             numericInput("n", label="Sample size per group", value=20, min=0, max=1000),
             br(),
             p("Population standard deviations:"),
             sliderInput("s1", label="Group 1", value=2, min=1, max=20),
             sliderInput("s2", label="Group 2", value=2, min=1, max=20),
             sliderInput("s3", label="Group 3", value=2, min=1, max=20)))
    ),

      column(9, wellPanel(
      numericInput("nsim", label="Number of samples", value=1, min=1, max=1000),
      actionButton("go", label = "Draw samples"),
      actionButton("clear",label="Reset Inputs"),
      textOutput("numsims")
    ))
  )
)

get.f.stat = function(y,x)  return(anova(lm(y~x))[[4]][1])

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  draw.sample <- reactiveValues()
  
  observe({
    if(input$go==0) {
      y=matrix(rnorm(3*input$n*input$nsim, mean=0, sd=rep(c(input$s1,input$s2,input$s3), each=input$n)), nrow=input$nsim) 
      draw.sample$y = y
      draw.sample$sample.means = apply(y,1,mean)
      
      x=rep(c("a","b","c"), each=input$n) ## create grouping variable
      
     draw.sample$f.stats = apply(y,1,get.f.stat,x)
            
    } else {
      y=matrix(rnorm(3*isolate(input$n)*isolate(input$nsim), mean=0, 
                     sd=rep(c(isolate(input$s1),isolate(input$s2),isolate(input$s3)), each=isolate(input$n))),
               nrow=isolate(input$nsim))
      draw.sample$y = y
      draw.sample$sample.means = c(apply(y, 1, mean), isolate(draw.sample$sample.means))
      x=rep(c("a","b","c"), each=isolate(input$n))
      
      ## THIS IS THE SLOW LINE:
      draw.sample$f.stats = c(apply(y,1,get.f.stat,x), isolate(draw.sample$f.stats))
    }
  })
  
  observe({
    input$clear
    draw.sample$y<-NULL
    draw.sample$f.stats<-NULL
  })
  
  output$y <- renderText({y})
     output$numsims  = renderText({  
       paste("Total samples drawn =", length(draw.sample$sample.means))
     })

})

Oops, I was entering 1000 in the wrong input box. It does take a few seconds on my computer.

But I think the problem is that the code just takes a long time to run in R. Here's a non-shiny version of the code in question - it also takes a few seconds on my computer.


input <- list(
  n = 20,
  s1 = 2,
  s2 = 2,
  s3 = 2,
  nsim = 1000
)

get.f.stat <- function(y,x)  return(anova(lm(y~x))[[4]][1])

y <- matrix(rnorm(3*input$n*input$nsim, mean=0,
               sd=rep(c(input$s1,input$s2,input$s3), each=input$n)),
         nrow=input$nsim)

x <- rep(c("a","b","c"), each=input$n)

system.time(
  apply(y, 1, get.f.stat, x)
)
#    user  system elapsed 
#   2.522   0.000   2.522

The below ui and server have hopefully minimal code (plots excluded) to show what is going on.  I wrote a comment above the one line that slows down the code.  If you comment out that line, and request 1000 samples, your request is processed instantly, but without commenting out that line, it takes 3-4 seconds.  I would love any insight into why this process is so slow and whether there are ways it can be sped up.  


shinyUI(fluidPage(

  titlePanel("ANOVA F-test"),
  fluidRow(
    column(3,
           wellPanel( 
             h5("Specifications for ANOVA:"),
             br(),
             numericInput("n", label="Sample size per group", value=20, min=0, max=1000),
             br(),
             p("Population standard deviations:"),
             sliderInput("s1", label="Group 1", value=2, min=1, max=20),
             sliderInput("s2", label="Group 2", value=2, min=1, max=20),
             sliderInput("s3", label="Group 3", value=2, min=1, max=20)))
    ),

      column(9, wellPanel(
      numericInput("nsim", label="Number of samples", value=1, min=1, max=1000),
      actionButton("go", label = "Draw samples"),
      actionButton("clear",label="Reset Inputs"),
      textOutput("numsims")
    ))
  )
)

get.f.stat = function(y,x)  return(anova(lm(y~x))[[4]][1])

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  
  draw.sample <- reactiveValues()
  
  observe({
    if(input$go==0) {
      y=matrix(rnorm(3*input$n*input$nsim, mean=0, sd=rep(c(input$s1,input$s2,input$s3), each=input$n)), nrow=input$nsim) 
      draw.sample$y = y
      draw.sample$sample.means = apply(y,1,mean)
      
      x=rep(c("a","b","c"), each=input$n) ## create grouping variable
      
     draw.sample$f.stats = apply(y,1,get.f.stat,x)
            
    } else {
      y=matrix(rnorm(3*isolate(input$n)*isolate(input$nsim), mean=0, 
                     sd=rep(c(isolate(input$s1),isolate(input$s2),isolate(input$s3)), each=isolate(input$n))),
               nrow=isolate(input$nsim))
      draw.sample$y = y
      draw.sample$sample.means = c(apply(y, 1, mean), isolate(draw.sample$sample.means))
      x=rep(c("a","b","c"), each=isolate(input$n))
      
      ## THIS IS THE SLOW LINE:
      draw.sample$f.stats = c(apply(y,1,get.f.stat,x), isolate(draw.sample$f.stats))
    }
  })
  
  observe({
    input$clear
    draw.sample$y<-NULL
    draw.sample$f.stats<-NULL
  })
  
  output$y <- renderText({y})
     output$numsims  = renderText({  
       paste("Total samples drawn =", length(draw.sample$sample.means))
     })

})
